# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_017_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 9

**1** "Anything else you want to see?" she asked when she was done. I was thrilled. "Yes, please, my lady!" **2** She laughed and said, "Take a good look at the seven women around the tower." "I see them," I said. "Good — this tower is being held up by those seven women. **3** The first, who is gripping the tower with her hands, is Faith. Through her God's chosen people are saved. **4** The second, dressed in a long beautiful robe, is Continence — the daughter of Faith. Anyone who follows Continence will be blessed in their life, because they hold back from all evil deeds, trusting that if they keep away from evil desires they will inherit eternal life." **5** "And the other five?" "They are all daughters of one another, each born from the one before: Faith, then Continence, then Simplicity, then Knowledge, then Innocence, then Reverence, then Love." **6** "What role do they play in people's lives?" "Here is the answer: anyone who follows these women and holds tight to their way of life will live in the tower alongside God's holy ones. **7** And why are they called daughters of one another? Because Continence comes from Faith; Simplicity from Continence; Innocence from Simplicity; Reverence from Innocence; Knowledge from Reverence; and Love from Knowledge. Their works are utterly pure, holy, and divine."

---

*PNEUMA note: "Love" used instead of "Agape" — the meaning in context is clear, and rendering it as "Love" at the culmination of the virtue chain gives it the most emotional weight for modern readers.*
